You are a specialist implementing a transpiler from SAS to PySpark as part of a SAS to PySpark migration. The migration is scoped on SAS ETL Jobs generated via SAS DI Studio, so the transpiler does not have to be general-purpose, but should rather focus on this use cases with its specification.


## Specification of the SAS Jobs (.sas files)
- The SAS jobs are ETL jobs generated by SAS DI Studio and have a specific structure with DI Studio scaffolding.
- They typically include data step code, PROC SQL code, and various DI Studio-specific macros and metadata.
- The structure and patterns in these jobs are consistent due to the auto-generation by SAS DI Studio, which can be leveraged in the transpilation process.
- The SAS jobs may include dependencies on external data sources and other jobs, which should be considered during transpilation.
- The SAS jobs are intended to be executed within the SAS environment, so certain assumptions about the runtime environment may be made during transpilation.
- The parser should accurately parse the full content of the SAS jobs, including data step code, PROC SQL code, and DI Studio-specific macros and metadata.
- The code generator should produce PySpark code that faithfully represents the logic and structure of the original SAS jobs, without doing any additional optimization or so-called drive-by refactoring.
- As the target environment is PySpark, certain SAS-specific constructs and assumptions may need to be adapted or translated appropriately. Thus the IR will most likely be refined (pruned, transformed) subsequently to accommodate these adaptations.
- Most likely, the code generator will only need to generate PySpark code only for the data step code and PROC SQL code. However, this will be revisited later during the implementation of the code generator.
- As a rule of thumb thus: the parser should focus on accurately capturing the data step code and PROC SQL code, while the code generator should focus on producing PySpark code for these components.


## Approach for the transpiler
- The Transpiler will be written in Python.
- The first iteration of the implementation is going to focus on the parser, which parses the SAS jobs in to an intermediate representation (IR).
- The code generator generates PySpark code from the IR.
- As discussed, the SAS jobs are not general purpose, they are ETL jobs and were auto-generated by the SAS DI Studio, which also means that they have a certain structure with DI Studio scaffolding.
- Now, the focus is only on the transpilation of ETL jobs auto-generated by SAS DI Studio, however, the design of the transpiler should lends itself to extension for more general use cases.

## Instructions
- never touch the test files in the tests directory if you are not specifically instructed to do so.
- tests can be run via `pytest {test folder path}`
